extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system (programmers, mathematicians doing computational algebra)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for creating, querying, mutating, and combining Magma aggregate data structures (enumerated sequences, lists, tuples, Cartesian products, coproducts, formal sets, records) and for using related constructors and intrinsics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prune(Q) / Prune(~Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: The function Prune(Q) or the procedure Prune(~Q) removes the last term from the sequence Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: print Prune(q2) returns q2 with final term removed. Use the procedure form (~) to mutate the existing sequence in-place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Append(Q, x) / Append(~Q, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Append places the object x at the end of sequence Q; the function returns a new sequence, the procedure mutates Q in-place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Append always appends x whether or not x is already present (duplicates allowed). Examples show Append(~q2, 99) and Append(~q2, 70) producing duplicate 70.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include(Q, x) and Exclude(Q, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and Exclude intrinsics for sequences: Include places x on the end if necessary; Exclude removes occurrences (semantics discussed earlier in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vs Append: Include generally ensures membership (no duplicate) semantics described earlier in Section 6.3.3; Exclude removes occurrences (e.g., first occurrence for enumerated sequences). Use function form to return a new sequence or procedure form (~) to mutate in-place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position(Q, x) / Index(Q, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Position(Q, x) or Index(Q, x) returns the index (position) of the first occurrence of x in Q, or zero if x is not in Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to locate elements before operations like Remove or Insert; examples reference Index/Position when explaining Q[i] assignment and multi-indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q[i] assignment (mutating a term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning to Q[i] changes the ith term of an enumerated sequence Q: Q[i] := x sets the ith entry to x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fr[6] := 99997 changes the sixth term. Indices must be in valid range; use mutation assignment to change elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explode(Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explode(Q) is a multiple-return-value function that returns Q[1], Q[2], …, Q[#Q], allowing assignment of sequence terms to identifiers in a single statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: z1, z2, z3 := Explode([8,7,6]); or partial unpacking first, second, _, _, fifth := Explode(fr). Useful to avoid many separate indexing accesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequence selection Q[I] and arithmetic progression abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Q[I] returns a sequence formed by selecting positions given by the integer sequence I; when I is an arithmetic progression, abbreviations Q[i..j by k] and Q[i..j] are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fr[[1,3,7,9]] or fr[2..8 by 3]. Note: Q[I] cannot appear on the left of an assignment to reassign several terms at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concatenation Q cat T and mutation cat:=
rubrics_metrics.description: Q cat T returns the concatenation [Q[1],...,Q[#Q], T[1],...,T[#T]]; Q cat:= T mutates Q by concatenating T to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: q2 := q1 cat [-3/7,...]; qq cat:= [100..400 by 100] mutates qq. Use cat:= for in-place modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsequence(Q, T) with Kind parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: IsSubsequence(Q, T) tests whether Q is a subsequence of T; the parameter Kind controls interpretation: default "Consecutive", "Sequential" (same order not necessarily consecutive), or "Setwise" (membership ignoring order and multiplicity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: IsSubsequence(q1,q2) true; IsSubsequence([9,6,3],[10..3 by -1]: Kind:="Sequential") true; Kind:="Setwise" tests set containment (same as Q subset T).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert(Q, i, x) and Remove(Q, i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert(Q, i, x) returns a sequence with x inserted at position i, shifting subsequent elements right; Remove(Q, i) returns Q with the ith term removed and following elements shifted left. Procedure forms (~) mutate in-place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Insert(q2,4,999) yields q2 with 999 at position 4; Remove(q3,4) can be used to undo an insert. Use procedure forms to alter existing sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert(Q, k, m, T) replacing range
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert(Q, k, m, T) inserts sequence T into Q replacing terms Q[k] through Q[m] inclusive; to insert T after m without destroying terms set k := m+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function returns new sequence; procedure form mutates in-place. Useful for bulk replacement/insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse(Q) / Reverse(~Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse returns Q with its terms in reverse order: [Q[#Q], ..., Q[1]]; procedure form mutates Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Reverse(y) shows effect. Use when order of elements needs reversing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotate(Q, p) / Rotate(~Q, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotate cyclically rotates the terms of Q by p to the right (if p >= 0) or -p to the left (if p < 0). The result is Q[(n-p+1)..n] concatenated with Q[1..(n-p)] for p >= 0 where n = #Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Rotate(~y,3) rotates y right by 3 positions. Negative p rotates left.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sort(Q) / Sort(~Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort returns Q with terms ordered into increasing order; available only when the universe of Q has a total ordering on its elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Sort(y) eq y_copy used to test if a sequence is already sorted. Use only for types with total ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-indexing (multi-dimensional sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: If elements of a sequence are themselves sequences, multi-indexing Q[i1][i2]...[ik] may be abbreviated as Q[i1,i2,...,ik] to access nested entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Q := [[40,50],[77,66,55],[],[150,250,...]]; Q[2,3] and Q[2][3] both return 55. Useful for treating nested sequences like arrays.

rubrics_metrics.name: rep{ x : x in E | condition } (rep-constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rep-constructor loops through iterable magma E and returns the first element x satisfying the condition; it avoids building the whole set and is more efficient in time and storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rep{g: g in Sym(5) | IsOdd(g)} returns first odd permutation. If the set is empty an error occurs; consider exists constructor when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: random{ x : x in E | condition } (random-constructor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The random-constructor returns a random element x of iterable magma E that satisfies the condition; available in multi-identifier form as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show random elements from S6 not in C6. If the described set is empty, Magma will give an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: exists{ x : x in E | condition } and forall{ x : x in E | condition }
rubrics_metrics.description: These constructors return boolean values: exists returns true if the described set is non-empty, forall returns true if the described set equals E. They iterate and may stop early when the outcome is determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: forall{sg : sg in SL | IsZero(ordS5 mod Order(sg))} checks divisibility property of subgroup orders efficiently. Use exists to test existence without risking an error from rep/random on empty sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: exists(d){ ... } and forall(d){ ... } witness/counterexample syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified exists/forall syntax with an identifier d assigns a witness element when exists returns true (d becomes that element), or assigns a counterexample to d if forall returns false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: exists(N){ n : n in [100..10000] | isperfect(n) } sets N to 496 when true. forall(k){ n : ... | isperfect(n) } returns false and sets k to a failing example (100).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal set constructor {! x in M | condition !}
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal sets represent subsets of a magma M defined by a boolean condition and are represented symbolically (not by enumerating elements), allowing infinite sets; operations are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universe(F) is M. Available operations include in, notin, join, meet, diff, sdiff when formal sets are compatible (implemented by boolean operations on conditions). Example: Zplus := {! n in IntegerRing() | n gt 0 !} prints as 'Formal set over Integer Ring'. Formal sets cannot generally be iterated to obtain elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists ([* *]) vs Enumerated Sequences ([ ... ])
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists are ordered, iterable, can contain repeated elements and heterogeneous element types; they are created with [* *] and are less efficient and have fewer operations than homogeneous enumerated sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: L := [* GF(8), "r", 1/3 *]. Principal operations: #L, IsEmpty(L), L[i], L[i] := x, concatenation L cat K and mutation L cat:= K, Append, Prune. Prefer enumerated sequences for homogenous data for efficiency and richer operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartesian product constructor car< M1, ..., Mk > and related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cartesian products represent tuples over component magmas M1..Mk. Functions include NumberOfComponents(C), Rep(C), #C (if finite), Set(C), Random(C), and Flat(C) to flatten nested Cartesian products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: CP1 := car< RationalField(), Booleans(), S6 >; Rep(CP1) yields <0,true,Id(S6)>. #C returns product of component cardinalities if all finite. Flat(C) returns base structures in depth-first order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuple creation: elt< C | m1,...,mk >, <m1,...,mk>, and coercion C!t
rubrics_metrics.description: elt< C | ... > constructs a tuple as an element of Cartesian product C; the shorthand <...> constructs a tuple and Magma deduces the parent product from entries; C!t coerces an existing tuple t into C when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: t1 := elt< CP1 | 3, true, S6!(2,4)(3,6) >. Coercion C!t succeeds only when component entries are coercible into components of C; otherwise runtime error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuples: fixed arity and component-parent constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a tuple t is created, its parent Cartesian product C is fixed: the number of entries cannot change and any new value for an entry must have the appropriate parent (component type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to set t2[1] := 17/23 when parent expects integers raises runtime error 'New component not in cartesian product'. You cannot iterate directly over a tuple (iterate over indices instead). Use Explode(t) to assign entries to variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explode(t) for tuples
rubrics_metrics.description: Explode(t) returns all tuple entries separately in index order (multiple return values), useful to assign tuple entries to identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ratl, bl, g := Explode(t1); prints individual components. Similar purpose as Explode for sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coproducts cop< S1, ..., Sn > and injections
rubrics_metrics.description: cop<...> constructs the coproduct C of constituent structures Si and returns C plus a sequence of injections [m1,...,m#C] where mi : Si -> C. Functions include Injections(C), Constituent(C,i), Index(x), Retrieve(x), Flat(C), UniversalMap(C,D,Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: C, m := cop< F25, Strings(), IntegerRing() >; use m[i](s) to inject an element or C!s when category is unique. Index(x) returns constituent index; Retrieve(x) returns the original si. UniversalMap constructs maps C -> D from maps Si -> D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat(C) for coproducts
rubrics_metrics.description: If constituents of a coproduct include coproducts, Flat(C) returns the coproduct of the base constituents in depth-first order and associated injections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates building CCC from C and CC and flattening to fCCC with constituents listed explicitly. Use to simplify nested coproduct structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: UniversalMap(C, D, Q)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given coproduct C with constituents Si, a target structure D, and a sequence Q of maps Si -> D, UniversalMap returns the universal map C -> D induced by those maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: constructing boolean test maps from each finite field component into Booleans and building um := UniversalMap(CC,D,qq) to test primitivity of elements across constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record format definition recformat<...> and record construction rec< F | ... >
rubrics_metrics.description: Record formats specify named fields and optional type/category constraints for each field; records of that format are created with rec< F | field:=expr, ... >. Fields may be left unassigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field expressions may evaluate to a parent magma (e.g., Sym(5)) or a category (e.g., RngIntElt) to restrict contents. Omitting ': expr' allows any type. Example: GroupInfo := recformat< gens, order : IntegerRing(), comment : MonStgElt >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record field access syntax r`f and dynamic field name r``s
rubrics_metrics.description: Access record field f of record r using the backquote syntax r`f. When field name is held in a string s use r``s (two backquotes) to evaluate s and access the corresponding field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the symbol is the backquote (`), not an apostrophe. Example: gC`comment prints comment; chosen_field := "gens"; gC``chosen_field accesses gens dynamically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record field assignment, assigned, delete, and Format/Names
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields may be assigned or left unassigned; assigned tests whether a field is assigned, delete deletes a field assignment. Format(r) returns the record format; Names(r) or Names(F) returns fieldnames as a sequence of strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: assigned gA`comment, assigned gB`comment returns booleans. Use these to manage and inspect record contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record field type enforcement and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma enforces simple parent/category constraints declared in recformat for the stored values (e.g., IntegerRing requirement), but does not validate complex invariants or that a field's contents meet semantic properties (e.g., set of all monic irreducible polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: recformat irred has prime and degree constrained but polys field only checked to be an enumerated set; Magma will not verify polys actually contains all monic irreducible polynomials of given degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: No built-in equality for records
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators eq, ne, lt, etc., are not available for records; equality would be application-dependent and the user should write a suitable equality function specifying semantics for unassigned fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If equality comparison is required, implement a custom function that defines whether records equal when some fields are unassigned or differ in unspecified ways.
